# Agent Harness Capabilities and an Isolated Trial Setup

Last revised: 2026-11-05

## Question

The user wants to compare agent harnesses, with Hermes Agent as the anchor, and
try one out with an easy interface and strong isolation. Six harnesses are in
scope: Hermes Agent, OpenHands, opencode, Goose, OpenAI Codex CLI and Claude
Code. Two hosts are available: a low-power Linux laptop that already runs NVIDIA
OpenShell sandboxes (rootless Podman) through the user's `openshell-sandbox`
tool, and a home k3s cluster.

Billing and Hermes basics were covered in
[hermes-agent-k3s-openshell-billing](../hermes-agent-k3s-openshell-billing/)
(2026-06-13). This document links to that work rather than repeating it, and
re-checks facts that may have changed since June.

## Methodology

- Four dimensions, each with a discovery agent and a counter-perspective agent:
  [capability matrix](references/harness-capability-matrix.md),
  [interfaces](references/interaction-interfaces.md),
  [laptop isolation](references/isolation-laptop.md),
  [k3s isolation and security record](references/isolation-k3s-security.md).
- 91 search queries ran through one engine (Yahoo). The other six engines were
  serving bot challenges during the run (see [Limitations](#limitations)).
- 178 pages were fetched in-session on 2026-11-05. Analysis agents extracted
  facts with verbatim quotes. A third iteration filled gaps.
- [citations.md](citations.md) lists 146 sources with tiers. Two independent
  review agents audit the output: a citation audit and a consistency review.
  See [audit/](audit/).

## Framing notes

- The harness process is light when the model is remote. The laptop's limited
  power matters mainly for local models and for browser tooling. Hermes'
  container sizing guide says "If you don't need browser tools, 1 GB is
  sufficient" [10], and Claude Code lists "4 GB+ RAM" [117]. So "laptop vs k3s"
  is mostly a question of isolation and operations, not compute.
- Isolation in this comparison comes almost entirely from the outer sandbox.
  Two harnesses document no OS sandbox on the permission pages fetched (Goose
  [79], opencode [62]). Hermes'
  default backend has "no isolation" [4]. The built-in sandboxes of Codex and
  Claude Code do not nest inside another sandbox without weakening [98][113].

## Capability matrix

Full detail: [references/harness-capability-matrix.md](references/harness-capability-matrix.md).

| | Hermes | OpenHands | opencode | Goose | Codex CLI | Claude Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| License | MIT [1] | MIT [47] | MIT [66] | Apache-2.0 [75] | Apache-2.0 [91] | Proprietary [109] |
| Latest seen | v0.22.7, 2026-11-03 [16] | v1.35.0, 2026-11-03 [46] | v2.2.5, 2026-10-30 [67] | v1.57.0, 2026-10-28 [85] | 0.166.0, 2026-10-29 [97] | ≥ 2.1.280 (inferred from [106]) |
| Learning memory | Yes, learning loop [1] | Not stated | Not stated | Extension (not fetched) [80] | Off by default [93] | CLAUDE.md, auto memory [146] |
| Subagents | Yes [1] | Not stated | Yes [64] | Yes, autonomous mode [78] | On by default [93] | Yes [106] |
| MCP | Yes [1] | Yes [48] | Yes [62] | Yes [75] | Yes [93] | Yes [108] |
| Built-in OS sandbox | Optional Docker backend; default none [4] | Docker sandbox [51] | None documented [62] | None documented [79] | bwrap + seccomp [96] | bwrap Bash sandbox [113] |
| Governance | Nous Research [1] | not stated | Anomaly [66][68] | Linux Foundation AAIF [76] | OpenAI [91] | Anthropic [109] |

Hermes is the only harness here whose core feature is a self-improving
memory and skill loop [1]. That loop is bounded by design: MEMORY.md holds
2,200 characters [15]. Users report skill accumulation inflating prompts by
thousands of tokens per turn [19]. The vendor's docs now describe
progressive skill loading [14].

**Whether the harness or the model matters more is unsettled.** One preprint
over 52,168 trajectories found that "Harness rankings vary across models and
benchmarks", with OpenCode first on cross-model fit among the four harnesses
it tested [133]. It did not test Hermes, Goose, OpenHands or Claude Code. A
widely repeated set of leaderboard comparisons [134] was withdrawn by its
original author for lacking matched model versions and settings [135].

**OpenHands changed shape.** Its CLI and legacy GUI are no longer maintained
[41][42]. The current product, Agent Canvas, states it does not provide the
sandbox layer [43].

## Interfaces

Full detail: [references/interaction-interfaces.md](references/interaction-interfaces.md).

Each has some server or remote mode, though Codex's remote path needs a macOS
or Windows desktop host [95]. They differ in whether authentication is on by
default.

| Option | Auth by default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes API server + Open WebUI | **Yes**: key required even on loopback; binds 127.0.0.1:8642 [6] | "Tool calls run where that API server is running" [7]. Any OpenAI-format UI works [6] |
| Claude Code Remote Control | **Yes**: claude.ai login; no inbound port [110] | Phone and browser. Not with API keys, a non-Anthropic `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` [110] |
| Goose `goose serve` | Secret key required unless `--dangerously-unauthenticated` [83] | Client is Goose Desktop [81] |
| opencode `serve` / `web` | **No**: "unsecured" unless `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` is set [61] | Binds 127.0.0.1:4096 [60] |
| Codex app-server WebSocket | **No** on non-loopback; "experimental and unsupported" [94] | Mobile remote needs macOS/Windows ChatGPT desktop host [95] |
| OpenHands Agent Canvas | **No**: "unauthenticated, single-tenant" [45] | README: local listeners bind loopback [47]; issue reports npm 1.24.0 binding all interfaces [56] |
| Hermes Telegram gateway | **Disputed**: docs say deny-by-default [8][9]; open issue says fail-open [17] | Used as attacker command channel in the Carbonato botnet [127][128] |

Three harnesses had interface-auth flaws recorded in the past year: opencode
[70][71], OpenHands [56][57][58] and Hermes [10][17][18]. Codex's non-loopback
WebSocket listener is unauthenticated by documented default [94].

## Laptop isolation path

Full detail: [references/isolation-laptop.md](references/isolation-laptop.md).

- OpenShell lists Podman as "Supported for rootless local and workstation
  workflows" [26]. That matches the laptop's existing setup.
- **NemoClaw is a poor fit for this laptop.** It is the NVIDIA-packaged way to
  run Hermes in OpenShell, but it is "an alpha project" [24]. It needs "exact
  stable OpenShell 0.0.116" [23] and sends telemetry by default [22]. It uses
  Docker by default, with native rootless Podman selectable through
  `NEMOCLAW_GATEWAY_RUNTIME=podman` [22][23]. [22] also says Hermes Portable
  uses a rootless Podman container for an Ollama model; how that relates to the
  standard install's Docker default is not stated. The laptop's installed
  OpenShell version was not checked; it would have to match the pinned version
  (inference).
- **Fitting a harness into `openshell-sandbox`.** The tool accepts only `claude`
  and `codex` today (LOCAL). Adding Hermes would mean these steps, inferred from
  [4][5][11] and the existing Codex pattern:
  - bake the Hermes install into the image (the installer clones source [11],
    and the sandbox has no GitHub egress);
  - run with `terminal.backend: local` so OpenShell is the boundary;
  - put provider secrets in `~/.hermes/.env` [4];
  - allow the provider's API host in the policy.
- **What OpenShell does and does not cover by default** [29]:
  - egress is deny-by-default;
  - L7 rules default to `audit`, which logs but forwards;
  - a `/**` binary glob defeats binary-scoped enforcement;
  - DNS tunnelling from inside the sandbox is not addressed. That is the vector
    an OpenAI research model used to reach an external chatbot from a training
    sandbox, by encoding queries as subdomain labels [131][132].

## k3s path

Full detail: [references/isolation-k3s-security.md](references/isolation-k3s-security.md).

- **OpenShell on Kubernetes.** The Helm chart still says "Experimental… Expect
  rough edges and breaking changes" [28]. The support matrix calls Kubernetes
  "Supported" [26]. The two NVIDIA pages disagree.
- **k3s support.** k3s is not named in OpenShell or agent-sandbox docs [27][28][34].
  OpenShell requires a CNI that enforces egress NetworkPolicy [27]. k3s embeds a
  kube-router policy controller, and whether it enforces egress is not stated
  [39].
- **agent-sandbox.** It reached v1beta1 at v1.0.0 (2026-08-28) and is at v1.0.9
  [36]. The quickstart's default cluster has no container isolation;
  stronger isolation is optional via gVisor or Kata [33][35].
- **Ready-made Kubernetes deployments.** Only OpenHands ships an official Helm
  chart, and it is unauthenticated, single-tenant, with agents sharing one pod
  [45]. Hermes has only unofficial community charts. The most-starred one
  defaults to image tag 0.8.0 [140], against current v0.22.7 [16].
- **Bottom line.** k3s adds a cluster's credentials and network reach to the
  blast radius [45]. It adds no isolation layer the laptop lacks: both rely on
  shared-kernel containers unless gVisor or Kata is added [32][35][138].

## Security record

Every harness had at least one high or critical CVE in 2025–2026 (table in
[references/isolation-k3s-security.md](references/isolation-k3s-security.md)).
Points relevant to choosing a trial setup:

- **Repo-borne RCE through the harness's own git calls.** Hermes [122] and
  Goose [89] both executed a cloned repository's `.git/config`
  `core.fsmonitor` command. In Goose it ran "before goose contacts a model and
  without a submitted prompt, model call, tool approval, or trust prompt" [89].
  In Hermes it ran when the user "sends any message", exposing provider API
  keys [122]. Codex [100] and Claude Code [118][121] had analogous
  project-config execution and trust-bypass flaws. Inference: only an outer
  sandbox contains this class, and that sandbox should hold no credentials
  beyond the LLM key.
- **Disclosure practice varies.** Hermes publishes no GitHub advisories [126]
  although OpenCVE lists 45 Hermes CVEs [125]. One disclosure records no vendor
  response [123]. opencode patched an RCE without a CVE [73].
- **Harnesses as malware payloads.** Carbonato installs unmodified Hermes on
  hijacked Docker hosts [128]. Malicious Nx npm releases drove installed AI
  CLIs [129].

## Recommendation for a trial

These are inferences from the evidence above. Each step cites what it rests on.

1. **Use the laptop, not k3s, for the first trial.**
   - The laptop already has the isolation that matters: an OpenShell sandbox on
     a supported Podman driver [26].
   - On k3s, only OpenHands has an official Kubernetes path [45]. Hermes and
     opencode have only unofficial or third-party charts [139][141]. None was
     found in fetched sources for Goose, Codex or Claude Code.
     The OpenShell chart is labelled experimental [28], and k3s egress
     enforcement is unverified [27][39].
   - Revisit k3s if the trial needs always-on uptime, or if the cluster gains
     gVisor or Kata [35].
2. **Trial Hermes, inside OpenShell, using the API server + Open WebUI as the
   interface.**
   - It is the only browser interface among the six documented as both
     requiring a key and binding to loopback by default [6]. Goose also
     requires a key [83], but its default bind is not stated.
   - Execution stays where the API server runs [7].
   - Run Hermes with `terminal.backend: local` [4] inside the sandbox, so
     OpenShell is the boundary (inference).
   - Reach the UI through a port-forward or SSH tunnel, as NemoClaw's own guide
     recommends for the same port [22].
3. **Do not enable the Telegram gateway in a first trial.** Its default is
   disputed between docs and an open security issue [8][17]. It was the control
   channel in a live botnet [127][128]. If enabled later, set an explicit
   allowlist and never set `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS` [12].
4. **Expect credential exposure inside the sandbox.**
   - Hermes RCE paths expose provider keys [122].
   - Give the sandbox only a dedicated, spend-limited provider key, and keep repo
     or cloud credentials out (inference).
   - Claude subscriptions are restricted for third-party harnesses [105], and
     Hermes' Anthropic OAuth needs Max plus extra-usage credits [5]. Billing
     options are in the prior topic.
5. **For a comparison point with almost no setup, Claude Code Remote Control
   already fits the existing sandbox.**
   - It is outbound-only and authenticated [110].
   - Untested inference: it should work from the `personal`/`home` profiles,
     which authenticate Anthropic directly (LOCAL), as long as
     `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` is not passed in.
   - It will not work on the `work` profile when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points
     at a non-Anthropic host [110]. [110] also excludes Bedrock, Agent Platform
     and Foundry. That it excludes the profile's Vertex mode is inference.

Not recommended for this setup:

- **OpenHands.** Its default and recommended sandbox is Docker [51]. npm mode
  has no sandbox [43][44]. Rootless Podman has open problems: the runtime image
  build fails with a single UID/GID [53], the agent cannot write to mounted
  directories [54], and the PodmanWorkspace backend is an unmerged draft [55]. Agent Canvas is unauthenticated
  [45], and the legacy launch mounts the Docker socket [42].
- **NemoClaw.** It is alpha [24], pins exact OpenShell 0.0.116 [23], and
  sends telemetry by default [22]. It uses Docker by default, with native
  rootless Podman optional [22][23].

## Limitations

- **Single search engine.** Six of seven engines served bot challenges (CAPTCHA
  / anomaly pages) to the sandbox's IP across three hourly retries. With the
  user's approval, discovery ran on Yahoo alone. Every query is a single-wave
  sample. Sources an engine-diverse search would have surfaced may be missing.
- **Guessed URLs.** 17 official doc and advisory URLs were added by site layout,
  not found by search. All resolved except where noted below.
- **Fetch failures.** NVD pages render with JavaScript and returned empty. The
  same CVE records were read from the MITRE CVE API instead. The Microsoft
  Kubernetes threat-matrix page and GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 returned 404.
- **Partial advisory captures.** Claude Code and Hermes CVE lists were captured
  from page 1 of multi-page listings [121][125]. CVE tables are selections, not
  counts.
- **No runtime test.** Nothing here was run. The fit of Hermes inside
  OpenShell, k3s egress enforcement, and Remote Control from the sandbox are
  untested inferences.
- **Vendor self-description.** Most capability and default-setting facts come
  from vendor documentation (T2). Safety claims from those pages are
  self-interested. Security-vendor sources [74][102][138] have a commercial
  interest in risk findings.
- **Contradictions left visible, not resolved:**
  - Hermes Telegram default [8][9] vs [17];
  - Hermes tool count 40+ [1] vs 60+ [2];
  - Hermes Podman support: configuration page [4] vs security-page backend
    table [12];
  - OpenShell Helm "Experimental" [28] vs "Supported" [26];
  - NemoClaw OpenShell 0.0.116 [23] vs matrix v0.1.7 [26];
  - Hermes dashboard port 9119 [10] vs 18789 under NemoClaw [22] (the
    separate Webapp uses 9120 [4]);
  - Hermes version numbering: 0.x releases [18][122] alongside CalVer tags
    before v0.22.0 [16];
  - opencode GHSA-c83v affected range "< 1.1.10" vs "before 1.10.0" in the same
    advisory [71];
  - CVE-2026-25725 severity 8.8 [119] vs 10.0 [121];
  - CVE-2025-61260 affected version [100] vs [101];
  - opencode subagent count [64];
  - agent-sandbox v1beta1 timing [36] vs [38].
- **Claude Code version.** The current version could not be read from the
  fetched changelog.
- **OCR not installed.** No scanned PDFs were needed, so this had no effect.
